paragraphs: A woman in layered worn clothing holds a handwritten cardboard sign, a figure that adds quiet humanity to a sidewalk or subway scene. The 67,087 polygons and 80,781 vertices cover her face, hair, the folds of coat and scarf, and the creased cardboard. Her posture is tired but steady, which keeps the scene respectful rather than melodramatic.

Non-overlapping UVs leave the sign surface clear, so you can letter your own message on it in any language. Her StemCell status means the coat, scarf and skin shaders were checked to match in every supported renderer. Muted browns and grays suit the outfit, and the cardboard can show water stains for a rainy street.

Two versions are priced at $69: this figure and a Seated Homeless Woman Holding Sign for wall or bench spots. The seated version suits a doorway or a station corner, the kind of place such people often choose. A 2024 release, she fits social awareness films, city crowd scenes, news illustration and narrative adventure games.

A horizontal fire-tube steam boiler with a tall chimney stack anchors a power plant hall, factory yard or historic mill scene. Its 1,322,919 polygons and 1,348,277 vertices are spent on riveted shell plates, valves, gauges, walkways and the long flue. The stack rises well above the boiler body, so the unit reads as industrial even from far away.

Mixed UVs split the painted shell, the brass fittings and the sooty chimney so each can weather on its own. StemCell certification covers even this heavy asset, so the painted steel looks the same whichever supported renderer you use. Rust streaks below the rivet lines and heat discoloration near the firebox make the boiler feel decades old.

The standalone version costs $69, while a Steam Boiler Plant with Pipeline System version is offered at $129. The plant version adds piping that ties the boiler into a larger process layout across the hall. Dating from 2026, it serves energy industry presentations, engineering training, steampunk worlds and industrial heritage documentaries.

A gantry-style construction printer extrudes concrete layer by layer, building house walls on site the way new building technology promises. Its 1,152,900 polygons against 596,240 vertices are spent on the frame rails, print head, hoses and the ribbed wall pattern. The frame spans the building footprint, so the print head reaches every wall without moving the machine.

Non-overlapping UVs keep the steel frame, the nozzle carriage and the printed concrete separate for texturing. Ribbed concrete layers are the visual hook, showing exactly how printed walls differ from cast or brick ones. A pale gray mortar shader with fine layer lines sells the material instantly in daylight renders.

Both versions are $69: the standard printer and a black rigged version ready for movement along its rails. The rigged version helps when a timelapse must show walls rising layer after layer on an empty plot. Out since 2024, the printer suits construction technology explainers, architecture presentations, futuristic city scenes and engineering education.

A hard hat fitted with a hinged face shield sits on a head, the protective setup for grinding, chemical work and electrical maintenance. The 67,777 polygons and 66,439 vertices cover the ribbed shell, the clear visor, the bracket hinges and the head underneath. The shield covers the whole face, showing viewers the level of protection a demanding task requires.

Mixed UVs separate the shell, the transparent shield and the head, so a scratched visor or company decal can be added. As a StemCell item, it comes with shaders checked for every supported package. At 33.93 x 31.25 x H43.53 cm, the hat and head fit a standard adult figure without any scaling.

This version costs $69, and a Power Utility Worker Protective Uniform with Safety Helmet version dresses a full figure for $129. The uniform version suits a complete lineman or substation worker when a whole body is needed in frame. Introduced in 2025, the hat fits workplace training, industrial visualization, utility company videos and factory games.

A stealthy anti-ship cruise missile with faceted body panels and folding wings skims low over waves in naval strike scenes. Just 13,331 polygons and 13,442 vertices carry the angular nose, wings, tail fins and the rear section. Its faceted shape is meant to scatter radar, and that geometry reads clearly even at a distance.

Mixed UVs let the gray radar-absorbing finish and the warning markings be painted separately. The missile is a StemCell asset, meaning its prepared materials give matching results across the supported packages. At 397.4 x 140.0 x H50.95 cm, it fits on deck launchers and coastal truck racks alike.

Two versions are offered: the Kongsberg NSM Anti Ship Weapon at $69 and a Naval Strike Anti Ship Missile Guided Weapon at $89. Mixing both versions gives a salvo some visual variety in long tracking shots over open water. Since 2026 the missile has served naval documentaries, defense analysis visuals, war games and simulator content.

A steel grey wristwatch with a moonphase window and leather strap brings refined detail to a desk flat lay or a close wrist shot. The 58,610 polygons and 65,117 vertices go into the case, crown, hands, sub-dials and the stitched curve of the strap. The strap curves as if wrapped around a wrist, so the piece looks worn rather than lying flat.

Non-overlapping UVs keep the dial printing, leather grain and brushed steel apart for sharp close-up texturing. Made to CheckMate specification, it measures 4.68 x 6.98 x H7.36 cm, true to a real watch on a wrist. The moon disc is the hero detail, so a soft top light that reveals its color works best.

Each of the two versions costs $69: this Leather Strap Moonphase Watch Steel Grey and a Patek Philippe Nautilus moonphase calendar version on leather. Pick the steel grey version for neutral styling and the named calendar watch for collector scenes. The watch arrived in 2025 and suits luxury e-commerce, jewelry store displays, gentleman's study interiors and character accessories.

A coastal anti-ship cruise missile with a booster stage and folding fins shows the weapon in launch-ready form. The 78,484 polygons and 77,804 vertices go into the cylindrical body, cruciform wings, air intake and tail fins. Its long body and rear booster make it unmistakable in side views over open water.

Mixed UVs split the camouflage body, stencil markings and the booster so each part can weather differently. Because it went through StemCell, the camouflage and metal shaders arrive tuned for each supported render engine. At 216.92 x 852.55 x H215.06 cm, the missile is long enough to fill a launcher tube on a truck.

At $69 you get either version: this Ukrainian-designed Neptune missile or a Naval Strike Guided Missile with Folding Fins. Coastal battery scenes often need several missiles, and the light mesh of either version allows that. New in 2026, it fits defense news graphics, military history documentaries, coastal battle scenes and war games.

A wooden market stall under a striped canvas awning, stacked with crates, sets up a street market, harbor bazaar or village fair. Only 22,468 polygons and 23,604 vertices build the timber frame, awning folds and crates, so many stalls can line one street. Slanted awnings throw shade on the counter, inviting a merchant figure to stand underneath.

Non-overlapping UVs let the awning stripes change color, red and white for a seaside market or green for a farm stand. Being StemCell certified, the stall shows the same timber and fabric look in every supported renderer. Crates sit at the front edge, where produce, fish or pottery can be added to tell what the vendor offers.

The stall has two versions at $69: this striped one and a Medieval Market Stand with Barrels for fantasy towns. Mixing both versions along one lane makes a market that feels assembled over years by different traders. Available since 2024, the stall fits historical games, film set extensions, festival scenes and travel illustration.

Contemporary chairs with clean lines, molded seats and slim legs furnish a dining room, cafe or office lounge from a single purchase. Mixing shapes around one table is a current design habit, and the varied silhouettes here make that easy. Upholstered pieces sit beside hard plastic and wood forms, giving an interior a curated rather than catalog look.

Each chair cleared TurboSquid's CheckMate Pro review, so topology and file structure hold up in close renders. Fabric, leather and lacquer shaders all suit these pieces, and color swaps take minutes with clean material groups. Soft shadows under the seats ground each chair on wood, concrete or tiled floors in daylight scenes.

Two versions are available: this first collection at $69 and Modern Chairs Collection 2 at $79 with further designs. Designers often test several chair styles around one table before committing, and both versions speed that up. Listed since 2022, the chairs serve interior design renders, furniture showrooms, real estate staging and architectural animations.

A hydraulic lift table raises a motorcycle or quad to working height, the centerpiece of any powersports repair shop. The 85,002 polygons and 88,597 vertices go into the steel deck, scissor frame, wheel chock, ramp and lifting mechanism. Workshop owners know this tool as the thing that saves backs during long engine jobs.

Non-overlapping UVs keep the painted deck, rubber pads and chrome hydraulics on separate map areas. TurboSquid rated the lift table CheckMate Pro, its top certification for geometry, scale and file organization. Oil stains and scuffs on the deck suggest a busy shop rather than a polished showroom floor.

Two versions exist: the static table at $69 and a rigged version at $79 that can be raised in animation. A bike clamped on top of either version makes a convincing service scene in a few seconds. Released in 2021, it fits garage interiors, motorcycle repair tutorials, dealership service bays and mechanic games.

A pair of anthracite black sneakers with a tall visible air sole rests in an open shoebox, the unboxing moment sneaker fans know well. The 55,079 polygons and 56,075 vertices cover the knit uppers, the full-length air units, laces and the box with its lid. The open lid frames the shoes, giving the shot the feel of a fresh delivery.

Non-overlapping UVs keep mesh, sole and cardboard on separate maps, so the box print stays crisp. The clear sole rewards a refractive shader, which lets light pass through and glow on the floor below. Its clean geometry follows CheckMate specification, holding up in macro shots of the transparent air bubble.

Editorial Uses Only terms apply here, so the shoes suit sneaker news, collector articles, reviews and fashion history content. There are two versions, each at $69: the black Nike Air 720 in Box and a white version in the same packaging, both from 2024. The white version suits bright, clean scenes, while the black pair sits better on dark shelves.

Everyday office machines and desk gadgets stock a workspace from the reception counter to the copy room in a single go. Boxy machines and slim desk devices are exactly what makes an empty office render look like people work there. Every piece sits at real desk height, so it lines up with chairs and monitors from other packs.

Every device in the bundle reached CheckMate Pro, the strictest certification TurboSquid hands out for geometry and files. Matte gray plastics with small status lights suit these devices, and a light dusting hints at long use. Cables can run along desk edges for realism, or be skipped for a tidy showroom look.

The bundle comes in two versions: this one at $69 and Office Equipment Collection 2 at a higher $119. Facility planners use either version to preview how equipment fits into a new floor layout before moving in. Part of the catalog since 2021, it supports workplace interiors, corporate training videos, office simulation games and architectural visualization.

A white curtain-sided semi-trailer with sliding side canvases lets forklifts load pallets from the side at busy distribution yards. The 103,150 polygons and 105,692 vertices cover the frame posts, tensioning straps, rear doors, landing gear and axle group. Strap buckles along the lower edge are the giveaway of this trailer type in road scenes.

Non-overlapping UVs give the canvas panels their own space, so a fleet design or a plain color is easy to apply. TurboSquid's StemCell program prepared its materials, so the white body renders alike in several applications. Built at full road size, the trailer lines up with loading docks and tractor units from other packs.

Two versions share a $69 price: this covered model and a black Curtain Trailer Without Canvas that shows the bare structure. The open frame version is handy for loading scenes where pallets and cargo straps must stay visible. Published in 2025, it fits logistics videos, highway traffic, port and warehouse renders, and truck driving games.

Carved tables in dark lacquered wood bring the calm of an Asian tea room, a temple hall or a traditional restaurant into a scene. Curved legs, inlaid tops and ornamental aprons give each table its own character, so a room never looks repetitive. Placed with cushions or chairs around them, the tables set up dining or tea ceremony scenes easily.

StemCell preparation means the lacquered wood and carved details render with matching shaders in each supported package. A warm red-brown finish with soft highlights suits these pieces, especially under paper lantern light. Fine wear on the corners and tops suggests furniture handed down through generations of the same household.

You can choose between two versions: this collection at $69 and Oriental Wooden Tables Collection 2 at $79. Together the two versions furnish a whole restaurant floor with tables of different shapes and sizes. Added in 2025, the set serves interior visualization, period drama sets, martial arts films and historical games.

A warm autumn outfit for a young girl dresses a character for chilly park walks, school mornings and leaf-strewn countryside scenes. Most of the 162,378 polygons and 194,480 vertices go into soft folds, seams, cuffs and the layered collar of the outer garment. Loose sleeves and a slightly oversized fit read as real children's clothing rather than a scaled-down adult outfit.

Non-overlapping UVs let you swap plaid, corduroy or knit textures across the pieces without stretching. Made in line with CheckMate specification, the garments open cleanly and fit a child-sized figure. Earthy mustard, rust and olive tones suit the season, matching falling leaves in an October scene.

Two versions cost $69 apiece: this clothing set and the Outdoor Autumn Clothes for Girl Fur version with fluffy trims. The fur version adds soft volume, which suits colder late-autumn shots with frost on the grass. Since its 2025 debut, the outfit has suited children's fashion visuals, animated films, picture book art and family games.

Sculpted pharaoh heads with striped nemes headdresses and ceremonial beards bring ancient royalty into a museum or tomb scene. Each face carries its own features and crown details, so a row of busts reads as different rulers rather than copies. Placed on plinths under spotlights or half-buried in sand, the heads suit both exhibition and adventure framing.

The heads carry CheckMate Pro certification, which means TurboSquid inspected their topology and scene setup closely. Gold leaf, painted limestone or weathered granite all suit the sculpts, depending on whether a scene needs glory or ruin. Deep carved stripes on the headdress catch raking light beautifully, adding drama to torch-lit tomb interiors.

Two versions are listed: the Pharaoh Heads Collection at $69 and Pharaoh Heads Collection 2 at $129 with further rulers. Pairing both versions lets a museum hall present a whole dynasty instead of a single king. From 2023 onward the heads have appeared in history documentaries, museum displays, adventure games and educational animations.

Bite-sized picnic snacks threaded on wooden skewers fill a buffet table, garden party platter or summer barbecue spread. Colorful layers on each stick make the food read clearly from above, the angle most party scenes use. Arranged in rows on a board or stuck into a melon, the skewers give a table instant festive variety.

Built to CheckMate specification, the snacks keep clean shapes that stay light even when dozens sit on one plate. Glossy shaders on fruit and matte ones on bread and cheese add appetizing contrast under warm light. Natural wood grain on the skewers ties the food to rustic boards, baskets and checkered tablecloths.

Both versions of the set cost $69: this collection and Picnic Snack on Wooden Skewer Collection 2 with other combinations. Caterers and food bloggers mix the two versions to plan a varied appetizer table before an event. Introduced in 2025, the snacks suit food photography mockups, catering menus, picnic animations and cooking games.

A portable karaoke speaker raised on a tripod stand brings instant party energy to a backyard, bar or living room. The 51,129 polygons and 53,649 vertices go into the speaker grille, control panel, handle and the telescoping tripod legs. Raising the speaker to head height helps sound carry over a crowd, a detail event hosts appreciate.

Non-overlapping UVs keep the grille, buttons and plastic housing separate, so colored lights or logos can be added. At 79.24 x 91.37 x H137.47 cm, the speaker and stand reach a believable chest height beside a singer. Glowing accent rings around the woofer set a party mood, especially in dim evening scenes.

This version and a PRONEXT Karaoke Machine on Tripod version are both priced at $69. The named version suits scenes that need a specific machine, while this one stays neutral for any setting. Launched in 2025, the speaker fits event planning visuals, music videos, home party scenes and karaoke bar interiors.

Grim fixtures and furnishings of a detention block gather in one set, ready to build a prison corridor or holding cell. Cold steel, worn concrete and barred openings give the pieces a harsh, institutional mood that reads at once. Lined along a corridor, the elements create the long repetitive perspective typical of prison films.

Under CheckMate Pro, the highest TurboSquid tier, the prison pieces were checked for clean topology and real proportions. Scratched paint, rust at the joints and graffiti on walls make the space look lived in by inmates. Harsh fluorescent light from above or a single window beam sets the tone for drama or horror.

Two versions exist for the bundle: Prison Space Collection at $69 and Prison Space Collection 2 at $99. Combining the versions gives enough parts for a full cell block, from intake area to solitary confinement. Since 2021 the set has been a staple of crime dramas, escape games, true crime reconstructions and film previsualization.

A welding helmet with a dark viewing lens sits on a head, the face protection every fabrication shop requires for arc work. The 36,766 polygons and 36,843 vertices define the curved shell, the lens window, the headgear ratchet and the head beneath. The helmet sits lowered over the face, the moment just before an arc strikes and sparks fly.

Mixed UVs split shell, lens and head into their own materials, so stickers, scorch marks or a custom paint job are easy. The helmet and head measure 20.85 x 25.37 x H33.06 cm, matching a full-size adult wearer. Following its CheckMate specification, the geometry stays tidy enough for close shots with sparks reflecting in the glass.

Two versions are on the page at $69: this Welding Helmet and a Speedglas branded version shown on a mannequin. The mannequin version suits product shots, while this one fits a working figure in a garage or shipyard. Brought out in 2026, the helmet suits welding training, metal fabrication videos, industrial safety material and workshop games.

A heavy rail adjustment tool clamps onto track and pulls rails into alignment, the kind of gear maintenance crews haul along the line. The 77,941 polygons and 80,806 vertices cover the steel frame, clamping jaws, hydraulic cylinder and carrying handles. Its long, low body sits across the rails, explaining at a glance how the machine grips and moves them.

Non-overlapping UVs allow chipped orange paint, grease and rail dust to be layered without stretching. Measuring 240.4 x 109.89 x H58.8 cm, it spans the track with room for crew hands at both ends. Weathered steel and faded safety paint make it look like gear that has spent years outdoors.

Alongside this version at $69 sits a Track Alignment Puller Orange variant at the same price. Rail safety films often show several tools in one shot, and the two versions fill that need. From 2025 the tool has served railway maintenance training, infrastructure explainers, rail yard scenes and engineering presentations.

Vintage gas pumps with rounded tops, glass globes and mechanical dials bring the feel of a mid-century roadside station into a scene. Bright enamel colors and chrome trim make each pump a strong silhouette against desert highways or small-town streets. Lined up under a canopy with a parked classic car, the pumps set an era in one frame.

Each pump holds CheckMate Pro status, so the meshes open cleanly and match real proportions. Faded paint, rust around the nozzles and cracked hoses suit abandoned stations, while glossy finishes suit restored ones. The glass globes on top can glow softly at dusk, a classic image for nostalgic poster art.

The collection has two versions: this one at $69 and Retro Gas Pumps Collection 2 at $89. Mixing pumps from both versions keeps a station forecourt from looking like copies on a grid. Listed in 2024, the pumps serve road movie scenes, diner exteriors, classic car renders and retro games.

A giant mechanical hand on a tall robotic arm towers over a workshop floor, built for heavy industry or sci-fi factory scenes. The 245,900 polygons and 253,059 vertices go into finger joints, hydraulic pistons, cable runs and the segmented arm column. Each finger is built from separate segments, which shows how the hand could grip a crate or a car body.

Mixed UVs separate the painted steel, chrome pistons and rubber parts so wear can be placed where hands touch. As part of the StemCell range, the arm comes with materials checked against several render engines. At 161.23 x 156.16 x H562.54 cm, the machine rises far above a worker, making the scale dramatic.

Each version costs $69: this clean build and the Robotics Mechanical Arm Module Yellow Old with worn yellow paint. The worn yellow version suits a scrapyard or abandoned plant, while this one fits a busy assembly hall. Industrial and sci-fi artists have drawn on it since 2025 for factory renders, robot films, mech games and engineering explainers.

Wooden and painted rowboats with oars, benches and weathered hulls fill a lake shore, fishing harbor or quiet river bend. Each hull has its own shape and color, so boats moored together look like a real working waterfront. Drawn up on sand or floating at a jetty, the boats suit both calm daytime and misty dawn scenes.

The set follows TurboSquid's CheckMate specification, so each boat opens with clean geometry and sensible naming. Peeling paint, wet wood and algae near the waterline make the boats look used rather than freshly built. Oars can rest inside or lean on the gunwale, small touches that tell whether anyone is nearby.

This first version costs $69, and Rowboats Collection 2 is offered at $79 with other hulls. Pairing both versions crowds a harbor with enough variety to avoid obvious copies along the pier. The boats date from 2026 and serve lake house renders, fishing games, period films and landscape paintings.

Steel scaffold frames, planks, braces and ladders assemble the temporary structures that wrap buildings under construction or renovation. Modular pieces stack and join like the real system, so a scaffold can climb one floor or a whole facade. Wrapped around a house or bridge pier, the frames instantly say work in progress to any viewer.

The kit meets CheckMate specification, keeping geometry clean when hundreds of tubes repeat across a facade. Galvanized steel with paint splatters and muddy footplates suits building sites, while clean metal fits a fresh setup. Safety netting or debris sheeting can be draped over the frames for a fully dressed site.

Two versions are available for $69 and $99: this Scaffold Collection and Scaffold Collection 2 with further parts. Combining both versions gives enough components to dress a multi-story site without repeats. New in 2026, the scaffolding suits construction visualizations, renovation explainers, urban scenes and building games.

A tracked self-propelled howitzer in camouflage paint carries a long-barreled artillery gun on an armored hull, ready for battlefield scenes. The 146,895 polygons and 159,437 vertices go into the turret, barrel, muzzle brake, track links and road wheels. The long barrel overhangs the front hull, a silhouette that reads instantly as artillery rather than a tank.

Overlapping UVs keep the repeated track links and wheels efficient, sharing texture space across the hull. StemCell work on this vehicle means the camouflage paint renders identically across the supported applications. At 201.77 x 997.14 x H258.46 cm, the vehicle dwarfs crew figures standing beside the tracks.

The page holds two versions at $69: this Self-Propelled Howitzer Weapon System and a Military Artillery Gun Mount Desert. The desert version suits sandy terrain, while the camouflage one blends into forest and field maps. First listed in 2025, it supports military documentaries, war games, defense presentations and simulation training.

A white zero-gravity toilet with leg braces and suction hoses shows how astronauts manage a basic need aboard a space station. The 21,734 polygons and 23,152 vertices cover the seat, the foot restraints, the vacuum funnel and the hose connections. Leg braces hold the user in place without gravity, a detail that always sparks curiosity in museum visitors.

Non-overlapping UVs keep the white panels, metal fittings and rubber hoses apart for clean texturing. The unit spans 254.74 x 254.74 x H79.07 cm, sized for a compact module compartment. Its CheckMate specification build gives tidy geometry, useful for cutaway views of station interiors.

There is this version at $69 and a NASA Space Vacuum Toilet Module White version at the same price. The NASA version fits documentaries that need a recognizable agency look, while this one stays generic. Released in 2025, it serves space education, science museum exhibits, sci-fi films and space station games.

A red squirrel sits upright with a pine cone in its paws, fluffy tail curled behind, ready for forest and park scenes. The 23,653 polygons and 23,722 vertices form a light base, since the fur system carries most of the visual detail. Tufted ears and a bushy tail are what make a squirrel read at a glance, and both are prominent here.

Non-overlapping UVs give the fur a clean map for color, from russet on the back to cream on the belly. Made under CheckMate specification, the animal keeps a natural pose that sits well on a branch or a log. Soft backlight through the tail fur brings out its volume, a classic look in wildlife photography.

Two versions are priced the same at $69: the standard build and the Squirrel with Pine Cone Fur for Maya version. The Maya version saves setup time for artists who groom and render inside that software. Since 2025 the animal has served nature documentaries, children's animation, forest games and seasonal greeting cards.

A grass camouflage hunting suit covers a figure in leafy fabric, blending into marsh reeds for duck hunting and wildlife observation scenes. The 30,142 polygons over 19,406 vertices go into the jacket, trousers, hood and the textured grass-pattern layers. Loose cut and padded shoulders leave room for layers underneath, as hunters wear on cold mornings.

Non-overlapping UVs let the grass pattern be swapped for forest, snow or desert camouflage without remapping. This camo suit reached CheckMate Pro level, TurboSquid's mark for clean meshes and orderly files. Muted green and straw tones melt into reed beds, especially under the flat light of an overcast dawn.

Both versions cost $69: this grass suit and a Hunting Suit Forest Camo version for woodland settings. Switching between the versions lets one figure move from marsh to forest without new modeling. Out since 2022, the suit serves hunting gear visuals, outdoor films, survival games and nature documentaries.

Tailored suit jackets in several cuts and fabrics hang ready to dress business characters, wedding guests or a menswear boutique rack. Notched lapels, buttoned fronts and structured shoulders give each jacket a sharp silhouette even in background shots. Mixing colors and patterns across a group keeps an office crowd from looking like clones in matching uniforms.

Made to TurboSquid's CheckMate specification, the jackets bring tidy geometry suited to fitting on different body types. Wool, tweed and linen shaders all suit these pieces, with subtle sheen on the lapels for formal looks. Pocket flaps and breast pockets give space for handkerchiefs or name badges in event scenes.

Suit Jackets Collection is the first of two versions at $69, and Suit Jackets Collection 2 costs $109. Tailors and fashion students use both versions to compare cuts before building a full outfit. First listed in 2016, the jackets remain a reliable pick for business scenes, fashion visualization and character design.

Swim fins in several sizes and blade styles equip divers, snorkelers and lifeguards for pool, reef or beach scenes. Long blades, open heels and adjustable straps give each pair its own outline, easy to tell apart on a dock. Laid on wet sand or hung on a dive shop wall, the fins set a water sports mood instantly.

These fins were modeled to CheckMate specification, keeping clean shapes that suit both close-ups and background props. Bright rubber colors and matte black blades suit the set, with a wet sheen for poolside shots. Water droplets and sand on the blades help the fins belong to a scene rather than a catalog.

Two versions are listed at $69 and $79: Swim Fins Collection and Swim Fins Collection 2. Dive centers and swimming coaches use both versions in training graphics and equipment guides. The fins came out in 2026 and fit diving animations, beach resort renders, sports product visuals and underwater games.

Teenage boy heads with different hairstyles, face shapes and expressions give character artists a fast start on young male casts. Varied haircuts, from short crops to longer messy styles, keep a classroom or sports team from looking cloned. Each head ends at the neck, ready to join a body or sit on a bust for portrait renders.

CheckMate Pro sits behind every head in the set, covering topology, scale and naming checks. Skin shaders with light freckles or acne marks suit the age group and add realism in close-ups. Soft key light from the side brings out jawlines that are still forming at this age.

Teenage Boy Heads Collection 2 extends the range at $99, while this original version is $69. Using both versions gives a school scene enough faces for a full class without visible repeats. Since 2022 the heads have served games, animated series, educational apps and avatar platforms for younger audiences.

Modern toilets and bidets in wall-hung and floor-standing designs furnish a bathroom from a compact apartment to a luxury hotel suite. Smooth ceramic curves and concealed flush plates give each fixture a clean contemporary look in any layout. Paired as matching sets, the fixtures help a designer show how a bathroom works in real proportions.

The fixtures earned CheckMate Pro from TurboSquid, a grade that covers geometry quality and accurate size. Glossy white ceramic with soft reflections suits these pieces best, and chrome fittings add a little sparkle. Tile floors and walls around them benefit from matching grout lines, which ground the fixtures in the room.

Two versions of these fixtures are offered, at $69 for this set and $79 for Toilets and Bidets Collection 2. Mixing both versions lets an interior designer test different styles in the same bathroom plan. Listed since 2018, the fixtures serve bathroom design renders, real estate visuals, hotel interiors and plumbing catalogs.

Obstacle course elements such as walls, hurdles and climbing frames set up a military boot camp or a fitness challenge scene. Rough timber, ropes and worn rubber give the pieces a tough, used look that suits mud and sweat. Spread across a field, the obstacles create a course that characters can run, climb and crawl through.

CheckMate specification guided the build, so the obstacles open cleanly with sensible scale and naming. Mud splashes on lower beams and frayed ropes suggest heavy use, while fresh paint suits a new training ground. Low camera angles make the walls and frames tower over runners, adding drama to a race.

There are two versions: this collection at $69 and Training Obstacles Collection 2 at a lower $46. The cheaper version works as background filler, while this one anchors the main course layout. Since its 2024 release, the set has suited fitness videos, military training scenes, adventure games and sports event graphics.

Traditional Turkish string instruments with long necks, carved bowls and fretted fingerboards bring Anatolian music into a scene. Each instrument keeps its own body shape, from pear-shaped bowls to slender lutes, so the group reads as a real ensemble. Hung on a music shop wall or held by seated players, the instruments set a cultural tone immediately.

Their geometry meets CheckMate specification, holding fine details like tuning pegs and strings without clutter. Warm walnut and mulberry wood tones suit the bodies, with inlay patterns painted into the textures. A soft key light reveals the curve of each bowl and the glint of the strings.

This collection at $69 has a second version, Turkish String Instruments Collection 2, priced at $79. Musicians and museums use both versions to illustrate how the instrument family varies in size and shape. Dating from 2024, the instruments suit music education, cultural exhibitions, historical films and folk-themed games.

A twin-wheel nose landing gear with shock strut, steering actuator and drag brace shows the hardware an airliner rolls on. Its 711,076 polygons and 720,514 vertices in clean quads detail the tires, hubs, torque links, hydraulic lines and bolts. The strut stands extended as if bearing weight on a runway apron.

Mixed UVs separate rubber, polished chrome and painted steel so each surface gets its own material. StemCell testing confirmed that its metals and rubber look consistent in each supported program. At 127.43 x 115.94 x H212.26 cm, the assembly matches full size beside a maintenance technician.
